BRIEF HISTORY OF THE COLLEGE
Talibon Polytechnic College (TPC) was established by Municipal Ordinance No. 2017-07. This was signed by Hon. Mayor Restituto B. Auxtero on July 17, 2017.This was sponsored by Hon. Councilor Janette Aurestila Garcia and signed by Hon. Vice Mayor Cleto R. Garcia, SB Chairman.

On July 21, 2017, Mayor Auxtero, Councilor Janette A. Garcia with Treasurer Rosalina G. Felisilda and consultants Dr. Mario E. Rodriguez and Dr. Lolita D. Rodriguez went to CHED Region VII, Cebu to give the letter of Intent to Dr. Freddie T. Bernal.
On May 10-11, 2018, Dr. Virginia dela Peña, with five (5) other Regional Quality Assurance Team (RQAT) members inspected TPC Programs: Bachelor of Science in Agriculture, Bachelor of Science in Accounting Information System, and Bachelor of Science in Information Systems.
On May 24-25, 2018, another four (4) RQAT members came and inspected the Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and Bachelor of Arts English Language. All with positive and inspiring comments.
Compliance for the minimum requirements of CHED including the enrolment of 176 students during the First Semester, AY 2018-2019 were submitted for final scrutiny and approval or grant of Authority for the five (5) degree programs inspected by the RQAT.
CHEDRO VII Order Numbers 005 & 006, Series of 2018 granting Government Authority to Operate BA Political Science and BA English Language were issued to Talibon Polytechnic College, School of Liberal Studies on November 25, 2018.
On March 15, 2019 the three (3) remaining courses were granted Government Authority to Operate. Bachelor of Science in Agriculture, (Government Permit No. 001 Series of 2019); Bachelor of Science in Accounting Information System (Government Permit No. 002 Series of 2019); and Bachelor of Science in Information Systems (Government Permit No. 003 Series of 2019).
Talibon Polytechnic College was granted Certificate of Eligibility to avail of the benefits of Republic Act 10931 otherwise known as the Universal Access to Quality Education Act. It has complied with the requirements for Institutional Recognition by virtue of the Commission en banc Resolution No. 564-2020. The full recognition was granted last December 7, 2020.
Highlighting one of our most notable achievements by far on this journey is the attainment of continuous accreditation. We understand that this recognition is not just a badge of honor, rather it is a testament to our unceasing pursuit of educational excellence. Through rigorous self- assessment and tireless improvement, we aim to exceed the standards set by accrediting bodies, reflecting our dedication to raising the bar in education.
In recent years, our dedication has been acknowledged with great pride. We are thrilled to announce that we have been granted Institutional Recognition by the Commission on Higher Education, a significant achievement underscored by Commission en banc Resolution No. 564- 2020. This recognition serves as a reminder that our efforts are valued and our commitment to quality education is recognized on a national level.
Furthermore, the dedication of our administration, faculty, staff, and students has led to the acquisition of the Certificate of Program Compliance for all five of our esteemed programs. This is a remarkable feat that showcases the cohesion and excellence within our academic offerings. It is a testament to the hard work, innovation, and adaptability that define us as an institution.

ARTICLE I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Chapter 1 PRELIMINARY MATTERS
Section 1. This document shall be called and known as the “Talibon Polytechnic College Student Manual.”
Section 2. Coverage – This Manual shall apply to and govern all bonafide students in all level and curricula of Talibon Polytechnic College.
Section 3. Purpose – This Manual is intended primarily to serve as a guide to student conduct and matters affecting student life.
Section 4. Interpretation – All provisions of this Manual shall, in case of conflict or ambiguity, be interpreted in favor of the students.
Section 5. Definitions of Terms – The terms as used in this Student Manual are defined as follows:
TPC refers to the Talibon Polytechnic College.
President refers to the highest official of TPC
Director of Student Affairs and Services refers to the officer designated to oversee the operation of the different units in-charge of student personnel services in TPC.
Recognition/Accreditation means the authority to operate at TPC granted to student organizations by authority of the President.
Student Organization means a group of students bound by common organizational objectives through programs and activities. It includes any association, club, society, order or any other form of organized groups whose members are students of TPC.
Recognized/Accredited Student Organization refers to any student organization which after meeting all necessary requirements as prescribed under this Student Manual is granted the authority to operate by the President.
Student Supreme Government refers to the highest official body governing the student body politics.
Chapter 2 DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES
Section 1. TPC recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building and shall promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual and social well-being.
Section 2. TPC shall respect the inherent individual and collective rights of students subject to limitations as provided by law, public policy and acceptable customs and traditions.
Section 3. TPC shall protect and promote the right to quality education of all students and to take appropriate measures to make such education accessible.
Section 4. No student shall be discriminated against by virtue of his birth, sex, religion, socio-economic status and political beliefs and aspirations.
 Section 5. Students shall be guaranteed participation and initiative in matters affecting their well-being.
Section 6. All students shall uphold the academic integrity of TPC and shall conduct themselves in accordance with established rules and regulations and acceptable norms of society.
Chapter 3 STUDENTS’ RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS
Section 1. Rights – The following rights under the Philippine Constitution and the Education Act of 1982 shall be guaranteed to every bona fide student of TPC:
A. Rights under the New Constitution:
1. The right to due process of law;
2. The right to equal protection of the laws;
3. The right against unreasonable search and seizure and illegal arrest;
4. The right to privacy of communication and correspondence;
5. The freedom of speech and of expression;
6. The right to peaceably assemble and petition the government for redress of grievances;
7. The right to free exercise and enjoyment of religious profession and worship;
8. The right to information;
9. The right to form organization or associations;
10. The right to effective and reasonable participation in matters affecting their welfare and student life;
11. The right to academic freedom within the limitations as provided by law;
12. The right to suffrage;
13. The right to health;
14. The right to quality education;
15. The right to select a profession or course of study subject to fair, reasonable and equitable admission and academic requirements;
16. The right to a balance and healthful ecology in accordance with the rhythm and harmony with nature; and
17. All other rights guaranteed under the Constitution not mentioned above.
B. Rights under the Education Act of 1982:
1. The right to receive primarily through competent instruction, relevant quality education in line with national goals and conducive to their full development as persons with human dignity;
2. The right to freely choose their field of study and to continue their course therein up to graduation, except in case of academic deficiency, or violation of disciplinary regulations;
3. The right to school guidance and counseling services for making decisions and selecting the alternatives of work suit ed to his/her
potentialities;
4. The right to access to his/her own school records, the confidentiality of which the University shall maintain and pre serve;
5. The right to issuance of official certificates, diploma, transcript of records, transfer credentials and other similar documents within thirty days from request;
6. The right to publish a student newspaper and similar publications, as well as the right to invite resource persons during assemblies, symposia and other activities of similar nature;
7. The right to free expression of opinion and suggestions, and to effective channels of communication with appropriate academic and administrative bodies of the college;
8. The right to form, establish, join and participate in organizations and societies recognized by the school to foster their intellectual, cultural, spiritual and physical growth and development, or to form, establish join and maintain organizations and societies for purposes not contrary to law;
9. The right to participate in the formulation and development of policies affecting the schools in relation to the locality/ region, and nation through representation in the appropriate body/bodies of the school to be determined by the Governing Board; and
10. The right to be free from involuntary contributions, except those approved by their own organizations or societies.
Section 2. Obligations. A bonafide student of the College shall be covered by all obligations as a citizen mandated in the New Constitution and those stated under Education Act of 1982 as follows:
1. To render personal, military or civil service under conditions provided by law;
2. To develop patriotism and nationalism, love of humanity, respect for human rights and appreciation of the role of nation heroes in the historical development of the country;
3. To understand the rights and accept the duties of citizen ship, strengthen his/her ethical and spiritual values, develop moral character and personal discipline, critical and creative thinking;
4. To exert his/her utmost to develop his/her potential for service, particularly, by undergoing an education suited to his/her abilities, in order that he/she may become an asset to his/her family and to society;
5. To uphold the academic integrity of the school, endeavor to achieve academic excellence and abide by the rules and regulations governing his/her academic responsibilities and moral integrity;
6. To promote and maintain the peace and tranquility of the school by observing the rules of discipline, and by exerting effort to attain harmonious relationships with fellow students, the teaching and academic staff and other personnel;
7. To participate actively in civil affairs and in the promotion of the general welfare, particularly in the social, economic and cultural development of his/her community and in the attainment of a just, compassionate and orderly society;
8. To exercise his/her rights responsibly in the knowledge that he/she is answerable for any infringement or violation of the public welfare and the rights of others;
9. To strive to lead an upright, virtuous and useful life;
10. To love, respect, and obey his/her parents, and cooperate with them to maintain the family solidarity;
11. To respect the customs and traditions of our people, the duly constituted authorities, the aims of our country and the principles of democracy.
12. To help in the observance and exercise of individual and society rights, the strengthening of freedom everywhere, the fostering of cooperation among nations in the pursuit of progress, prosperity and world peace.
ARTICLE II ACADEMIC RULES, PROCEDURES AND REQUIREMENTS
Chapter 1 ADMISSION POLICIES
Section 1. Graduates of recognized private and public high school may be admitted to Talibon Polytechnic College without any regard of age, gender, religion or race.
Section 2. The Committee on Admission of the college is tasked to screen the credentials of the applicants.
Section 3. Talibon Polytechnic College reserves the right to refuse any applicant whose qualifications do not meet the standards of the school.
Chapter 2 ADMISSION TEST
Section 1. All applicants for admission to Talibon Polytechnic College for all the degree programs shall take the TPC Admission Test.
Section 2. The TPC Admission Test is a standardized test requiring careful attention to instructions and time limits. It is designed to provide convenient, objectively-scorable measure of general cognitive ability or intelligence in the form of a profile containing five verbal (Information, Comprehension, Arithmetic, Similarities and Vocabulary) and five performances (Digital Symbol, Picture Completion, Spatial, Picture Arrangement and Object Assembly) subtest scores.

Chapter 4
REGISTRATION/ENROLMENT POLICIES
Section 1. Registration of students shall only be on the regular registration period indicated in the academic calendar.
Section 2. A student must be officially registered in order to receive credit for course work.
Section 3. A student is considered officially enrolled when he/she has the Certificate of Registration duly validated by the Registrar.
Section 4. An admission slip/clearance or report of grades showing the scholastic standing of an old student is required as a credential for enrollment.
Section 5. A student is not allowed to enroll in more than one course during his stay in the College.
Section 6. Rules on sequencing of subjects (prerequisites) in a curriculum are observed and followed in enrollment.
Section 7. Registration of a returning student is dependent on his previous scholastic standing. All subjects taken from previous school where the same course description and units have been automatically credited.
Chapter 5 ACADEMIC INFORMATION
A. Academic Load
Section 1. The study load of a regular student is the number of units prescribed by the curriculum in which the student is enrolled.
Section 2. A student is considered full time or carrying a full load when he carries all subjects prescribed in his curriculum for a particular school semester.
Section 3. Students should follow the study load prescribed by his/her curricula or as assigned and approved by his/her respective Deans and Registrar.
Section 4. During Summer Term, a student may register only in nine (9) units, except for graduating students who shall be allowed a higher load not exceeding 12 units.
Section 5. Only graduating students are allowed to overload, subject to their academic standing.
Section 6. A graduating student may be permitted to carry a heavier load but not to exceed 27 units subject upon to the approval by authorities concerned.
Section 7. Students who are scholastic delinquents are not allowed to have an overload.
Section 8. Teacher Education students taking up practice teaching are allowed to overload or have other subjects taken alongside with practice teaching not more than six (6) units.
Section 9. Load of transfer students shall be limited only to those subjects without prerequisite, until such time this subject had already been validated/accredited.
Section 10. The Dean/Program Head may limit the academic load of student who are employed outside the institution whether full time or part time. (MORPHE guidelines, specifically Article XIX, Section 92, allow for a maximum overload of six units for graduating students, as stated in CMO 104, s. 2017, Section 12. A student intern can take other subjects with a maximum of six units during the internship period and/or according to the Institution’s
policy.)
B. Changing/Adding/Dropping of Subjects
Section 1. The students shall accomplish the prescribed form for changing, adding, and dropping after which he/she seeks the approval of the Dean.
Section 2. The Registrar shall determine the schedule for changing adding and dropping of subjects. (commonly, 1st week of the start of classes/ 5 days from the start of classes)
Section 3. The student shall then proceed to the Registrar’s Office for the issuance of the new Certificate of Registration
(COR)
C. Cross Enrollment
Section 1. The term cross-enrolment refers to simultaneous enrolment in two schools within a semester.
Section 2. No simultaneous enrolment in more than two schools allowed
Section 3. A maximum of six (6) units may be taken from the school provided by the total number does not exceed the prescribed units in the curriculum.
Section 4. Cross enrolment in other schools is allowed only when a student is a candidate for graduation or will do the internship/affiliation in the succeeding semester
Section 5. The graduating student must submit a letter of intent to cross-enroll at the Registrar Office noted by his/her respected Head and approved by the college Dean.
Section 6. The Registrar will issue a permit to crossenrolment approval and evaluation.
D. Shifting from Program to Another
Section 1. Shiftees leaving one program to transfer to another program within the college should accomplish the appropriate shifting form duly signed by the Program Heads, Registrar and VPAA.
Section 2. Shiftees are required to comply clearance from the previous department.
Section 3. Shiftees should request Student’s Evaluation from the Registrar and submit a copy to the Dean for proper loading of courses.
E. Withdrawal of the Course in the Program
Section 1. Talibon Polytechnic College recognizes the right of student to withdraw from their subject or course due to valid reason provided he/she must pay the amount due of total school fees:
1. within 1 week of class from start of classes 10%
2. within 2 weeks of class from start of classes 20%
3. after 2 weeks of class from start of classes 100%
F. Validation of Subject/Transfer of Credits
Section 1. A transferee student may apply for advanced credits or transfer of credits for work done in another Recognized Higher Education Institutions.
Section 2. Subjects taken from other schools must be evaluated for subject credits equivalent to TPC subject credits
Section 3. Course taken in other schools by transferees may be credited, provided that the number of units to be credited does not exceed 20% of the total number of units required in the program a TPC.
Section 4. Only the grades in the courses taken in TPC shall be included in the computation of the Cumulative Grade Point Average (GCPA).
Section 5. In order to graduate with honors, 80% of the total credits earned toward the degree must have been earned in residence at TPC.
Section 6. Courses taken from another school should be credited on the first term of studies at TPC. No other course taken from another school may be credited subsequent to this approval.
G. Pre-requisite of Subject/s
Section 1. The rules on sequence of subjects in the curriculum of the course being taken must be followed.
Section 2. Enrolling in and attendance in a subject without passing its prerequisite shall earn the student no academic credit.
Section 3. Waiver of Prerequisite. Graduating student shall be allowed to take the prerequisite subject and higher subject simultaneously with the approval of the Dean and noted by the College Registrar. However, if the student failed the prerequisite subject, the higher subject shall not be given credit. (CHED Memorandum Order No. 40. S, 2008, re: Manual of Regulations for Private Higher Education [MORPHE], Section 92, upon the discretion of the higher education institution, a graduating student may be allowed additional subject-loads of not more than six [6] academic units in excess of the normal load prescribed by the Institution for the last school term. Likewise, a graduating student may, on a case-to-case basis, be allowed to take several Physical Education [PE] courses in a semester. The request for two [2] or more basic PE subjects should include the following information:
1. Name of student;
2. Reasons justifying his failure to take PE in the preceding semesters;
3. The class schedule and the schedule of the requested PE classes; and
4. The endorsement of the Registrar with the statement
“Graduating upon completion of load.”
H. Request for the Offering of Non-Programmed Subject/s
Section 1. Subjects not scheduled for a given term may be offered upon written request of at least fifteen (15) students for the undergraduate duly endorsed by the Dean/Program Head and approved by the VP for Academic Affairs to be noted by the College Registrar. Exception to the number of petitioners may be allowed under the following conditions: 1. The student is graduating during the term;
2. When an old curriculum is superseded by the new curriculum;
3. Failure of the student to take the subject/s is attributed to the institution; and
4. The student is willing to pay fourteen (14) students fees with 175.00 per unit.
a. 3 units (subject units) x 175.00 per unit =
525.00 x 14 students = 7, 350.00
Section 2. The Vice President for Academic Affairs shall approve the request of non-programmed subjects provided that all provisions mentioned above are complied
Section 3. The approved offering of non-programmed subject/s shall be transmitted to the Office of the registrar to be entered into the System for the Official Offering.
Section 4. Procedures:
1. The concerned students, at least fifteen (15), shall write a formal letter addressed to the Vice President for Academic Affairs, and endorsed by the Dean/Program Head. Enumerated in the request letters are the names of requesting students, subjects requested, reasons of request and the instructor of the subjects.
2. The VP for Academic Affairs act on the request letter approved or disapproved.
3. When approved, copy of the letter request, endorsement and approval will be forwarded to the Registrar’s Office for System encoding.
4. The student will be issued the Certificate of Registration.

Affairs.
Section 2. The number of minutes for a student to be late is 15 minutes. More than 15 minutes, the student is considered absent but allowed to attend the class subject to existing rules and guidelines. The best Judgment of the teacher is required to help the student.

L. Residency
Section 1. Students' enrolment for residency to be classified and considered as bonafide students.

2. The student informs/contacts the Program Adviser that she/he is enrolling for residency: Academic/Non- Academic.

4. The student informs the Office of the College Registrar to facilitate the enrolment process for residency.
5. The Registrar's Office reviews the student's records before enlisting the student.

Section 2. The undergraduate residency comes in two forms-the Academic Residency and the Non-Academic Residency. Those who are on academic residency are deemed as bonafide students for the covered term. Students on residency will have their IDs validated for the covered term.

Section 5. A student on LOA may not enter the campus. As such, no residency, whether academic or non-academic, shall be granted to students on LOA. Students not enrolled but need to frequently enter the campus shall be required to enroll in undergraduate residency.
Section 6. Non-Academic Residency (NAR) is intended for students who need to enter the campus for co-curricular activities, as determined by the Dean of Student Affairs. The NAR is intended for the summer term only. A student, on his own, may not enroll for NAR. It is the Director of Student Affairs who initiates enrolment for NAR.

1. Credit units for each subject are multiplied by the grade earned to obtain the credit point per subject
2. The resulting credit points are added
3. The total number of credit points is divided by the total number of credit units to obtain the GWA. The GWA is then computed to two (2) decimal places
4. For GWA computation purposes, a descriptive grade of Failure or No Credit in any subject is equivalent to 5.00

U. Student’s Rights
Section 1. In addition to Section 9 of the Education Act of 1982, which grants students the right to access their school records and obtain official documents, other legal bases include the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173), which ensures students' control over their personal information, and the Civil Code of the Philippines, which protects privacy rights. The Family Code of the Philippines also reinforces privacy, especially when students reach legal age. These laws collectively guarantee students' rights to access and control their school records
Section 2. A student of legal age (18 or older) in the Philippines can deny their parents access to their school records. Under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173), individuals have control over their personal data, and schools must obtain the student's consent to disclose information to third parties, including parents, unless required by law. Once a student reaches legal age, they are the sole authority over their academic records, unless there is a legal basis for disclosure.
V. Issuance of a Certification, Diploma, or Record to a Proxy
Section 1. Under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173), personal data, including academic records, can only be disclosed to a third party, such as a proxy, with the explicit consent of the data subject, typically provided through written authorization. Section 9 of the Education Act of 1982 (Batas Pambansa Blg. 232) grants students the right to access their school records and obtain official documents, implicitly allowing them to authorize a proxy to secure these records on their behalf. Additionally, the Civil Code of the Philippines (Republic Act No. 386) permits the delegation of authority through a Special Power of Attorney (SPA), which is commonly required when a proxy is appointed to act on behalf of the student in obtaining academic documents.

Chapter 11 COLLEGE ADMISSION AND ENROLLMENT POLICY FOR PERSONS WITH DISABILITY
(PWD) AND SOLO PARENTS
Section 1. Purpose. The aim of this policy is to provide Persons with Disabilities (PWD) and Solo Parents with equal access and opportunity for admission, enrollment, and academic achievement at Talibon Polytechnic College. TPC endeavors to provide a diverse, inclusive, and caring learning environment for all its students.
Section 2. Scope. This policy shall be observed by all potential students applying for admission, and by those requesting enrollment or re-enrollment in degree and nondegree programs of Talibon Polytechnic College, whether or not they have disabilities or are solo parents.
Section 3. Policy Statement
1. Non-Discrimination. Talibon Polytechnic College adheres to the values of equal opportunity, nondiscrimination, and respect for diversity. The college believes in extending fair access to education to persons with disabilities and solo parents.
2. Persons with Disabilities (PWD). The college has a policy of reasonable accommodation for the PWDs as per the laws. The institution accepts that the PWDs have special difficulties and offers extra assistance to enable them to become fully involved in college life.
Section 4. Admission Requirements. PWD applicants will be judged on academic criteria only. The college will not apply extra requirements that are discriminatory and inaccessible to the PWDs.
Section 5. Reasonable Accommodations. The college will also make changes to facilities, services, and policy where appropriate. This might include, but is not limited to:
1. Accessible campus facilities (ramps, elevators, designated seating).
a. Altered examination procedures (extra time, quiet room, screen readers).
b. Supply of assistive technologies.
Section 6. Disclosure and Confidentiality. PWD applicants are encouraged to reveal their disability status at the time of admission for the school to know the possible programs specific for their needs. All personal data pertaining to the disability will be treated confidentially in accordance with applicable data protection legislation.
Section 7. Collecting the disability information about the student’s disability will solely be used for providing accommodations and support. This information will not be used for any forms of discrimination or deny opportunities.
Section 8. Solo Parents. Solo parents, as classified by the Solo Parents' Welfare Act (Republic Act No. 8972), are entitled to assistance during the admission process and through their entire academic life. The school acknowledges the balancing act between study and parental duties and strives to alleviate the solo parent students' burdens.
1. Admission Consideration: Solo parents who qualify for admission to the chosen academic program will be considered without prejudice. Priority scholarship or financial assistance consideration may be given based on single parent status, especially for those financially underprivileged.
2. Support for Solo Parents: Reasonable support measures will be made available by the college to help solo parents meet their academic requirements, such as:
a. Flexible class or examination schedules where feasible.
b. On-campus childcare access or help.
c. Counseling and academic as well as emotional counseling services.
3. Financial Assistance: The school will see if it is possible to extend scholarships, grants, or UNIFAST law for solo parent students. Aside from these, special payment arrangements can also be provided in order to soften financial loads.
Section 9. Application Procedures
1. For PWD Applicants: Applicants with disabilities who want to apply for admission must submit proof of disability issued by a licensed physician or a government agency accepted by law (e.g., PWD ID). This proof must be submitted to the Admissions Office during application.
2. Solo Parent Applicants: Applicants who are solo parents must provide evidence of single-parent status, i.e., Solo Parent ID or certification issued by the local government unit (LGU). The college shall validate this document to determine qualification for available accommodations or benefits.
Section 10. Support Services and Facilities
1. PWD Support Services: Disability Resource Center (DRC): The DRC shall serve as the central point of contact for PWD students to obtain accommodations and support services.
a. Accessible Learning Tools: Available on request like online platform (schoology), online and offline modules.
b. Personal Assistance: Where required, personal assistants or volunteers can be provided to support PWD students.
2. Solo Parent Support Services: Counseling and Peer Support: Academic and emotional support services will be offered to enable solo parents to cope with studies and family duties.
a. Childcare Services: The college will collaborate with local daycare centers or investigate in-campus childcare arrangements to assist single parent students.
b. Flexible Learning Options: Single parents can be given the choice of taking courses through online platforms or evening classes to fit their parental responsibilities.
Section 11. Monitoring and Evaluation: To facilitate effective implementation of this policy, regular monitoring will be done to assess the appropriateness of support given to PWD students and solo parents. Students' feedback will be eagerly sought and used for enhancing services.
Section 12. Grievance and Appeal Procedures: Any student who believes they have been denied proper accommodation or support can submit a grievance to the Office of Student Affairs or the Disability Resource Center (for PWDs). The process of appeal will ensure that grievances are heard promptly, equitably, and without reprisal.
Section 13. Review and Amendments: This policy will be revisited on an annual basis by the Office of Student Affairs, Admissions Committee, and other departments. Any updates or modifications to the policy will be notified to the student population and staff in a timely and regular manner.
Section 14. Talibon Polytechnic College ensures all students, irrespective of their disability status or family background, an equal opportunity to excel academically. The college, through this policy, attempts to provide a learning environment. Through this policy, the institution seeks to create an environment where every student can achieve their full potential.

Chapter 2 NORMS OF CONDUCT
Section 1. Every student must be imbued with patriotism and nationalism, love of humanity, respect for human rights, civic conscience, ethical and moral values, moral character and self-discipline in keeping with the man dates of the educational system under the Philippine Constitution.
Section 2. For the guidance of all concerned, the following norms of conduct and discipline of student are hereby promulgated, namely:
a. Moral Character. A student is imbued with moral character if among other qualities:
1. Has learned to act, live and think as a person whose values, attitudes and convictions are in accord with the Universal Ethical Norms of Right Reason and the accepted values and levels of conduct in the society where he lives;
2. Is honest to himself/herself, accepting his/her shortcomings and striving to improve or change them;
3. Is fair and just in his/her dealings with his/her fellowmen;
4. Lives by the precepts of love, justice, compassion and concern for other; and
5. Respects and defends the right of others as he/she wants his/her own rights to be respected and defended.
b. Personal/Self Discipline. A student is imbued with personal self-discipline if among other qualities:
1. Is devoted to the fulfillment of all obligations and considers his/her rights as a means for the fulfillment of such obligations;
2. Learns to forge the enjoyment of certain rights and privileges that others’ needs maybe benefited;
3. Resolves problems and conflicts without prejudicing others;
4. Is tolerant of others; humble enough to accept opinion that may be better than his/her;
5. Avoids vices, e.g. gambling, drinking alcoholic beverages, illegal drugs, sexual excesses and aberrations, etc. and
6. Guides and controls his/her life, actions and emotions.

a. During the period of suspension, the student shall be deemed divested of all privileges as a student of the institution and shall not be allowed to enter the premises of any campus or use any facilities of the college. The student ID shall be confiscated and deposited with the Director of Student Affairs and Services up on the execution of the order. Discipline officers or their equivalent shall be properly notified of students serving the formative intervention of suspension.

c. Any student whose suspension covers the final examination period will have to miss the final examination. In all cases of suspension, a written promise of future exemplary conduct by the student countersigned by his/her parents or guardian is required as a condition for readmission and shall be filed in his/her folio.

ARTICLE V ADMINISTRATIVE DUE PROCESS
Section 1. An administrative due process refers to the procedural fairness that schools must provide to students before imposing formative intervention like suspensions or expulsions. It ensures students are treated fairly and have a chance to respond to accusations. Key elements include proper notice of charges, the right to a hearing, and a decision based on evidence.
Section 2. Disciplinary matters are those acts of students referred to in the College Student Manual that need formative intervention through Warning, Reprimand, Suspension, Exclusion or Expulsion. It is conducted if there is a complaint, letter, report or memo pertaining to an alleged commission of an act by any student of the College that may be considered as a misconduct, offense, infraction or violation of a policy, rule or regulation of the College.
Section 3. The procedure is aimed at determining whether a student, who is under investigation for the commission of an alleged misconduct, offense, infraction or violation of any of the college policies, rules or regulations, is liable or not; and if so, the proper formative intervention shall be meted, but if not, the case shall be dismissed.
The procedure is as follows:
A. Complain report
Section 1. The complaint, letter, report or memo (hereinafter referred to as “COMPLAINT”) may be made by any concerned or interested party, such as a student, a trainee, a parent, an employee, an office head, an administrator, TPC itself, and others. The parent or guardian may also assist his/her child/ward or directly complain on behalf of the student.
Section 2. In the exercise of its management prerogative, TPC through any of its office heads may, motu proprio or at its own initiative, request for or initiate an administrative investigation of a student. Moreover, if warranted by circumstances, TPC through any of its office heads, particularly the program head or dean of the concerned or affected student or students, motu propio or acting upon a directive from a TPC higher official, may conduct an inquiry on any matter it may deem proper and necessary for fact-finding purposes, and if the results thereof require that a disciplinary administrative investigation be conducted, the office head concerned shall submit his/her memo or report with a request for such an investigation to be conducted by TPC.
Section 3. In fact, it is a serious obligation on the part of any College official or personnel to report immediately to his/her superior within 24 hours (personally or through memo or phone) or as soon as practicable any information or knowledge of an offense, wrongdoing, misconduct, or violation committed by his/her student.
1. Complainant. The complaint must be in writing and signed. As much as possible, the complaint shall provide the following information:
a. The name and residence, office or school address of the
complainant;
b. The name and residence, office or school address of the respondent; c. The substance, cause or basis of complaint;
d. When and where the act reported or complained of happened; and
e. The name(s) of any witness(es) thereto other than the complainant, if any.
2. Office/Personal to whom the case may be filed.
a. The complaint may be filed with the office of the President, Vice President, Student Affairs Services Director, Guidance Counselor or Immediate
Academic Head of the student to be investigated.
b. Any complaint, letter, report or memo of an act, violation, misconduct or infraction committed by a student of the College requiring a disciplinary administrative investigation received by any official shall be forwarded to the Immediate
Academic Head of that student. If the Immediate Academic Head is involved as the complainant or respondent, the complaint shall be forwarded to the Vice
President for Academic Affairs (VPAA).
3. Start of the Investigation
a. Upon receiving an information or knowledge, or upon receipt of such complaint, the Immediate Academic Head or VPAA shall do any of the following:
1.) If the complaint is sufficient to initiate a disciplinary administrative investigation (that is, the alleged facts are clear and there are available sufficient evidence), the Immediate Head will immediately refer the matter to the Director of the Office of the Student Affairs and
Services by way of a report or memo.
2.) If the complaint appears to be lacking clear factual allegations, parties involved and/or evidence, the Immediate Academic Head shall immediately conduct a fact-finding inquiry to further clarify certain matters, or obtain additional facts. If the initial findings establish a conclusion of a probable commission of the alleged misconduct, offense, infraction or violation that requires a disciplinary administrative investigation, he/she will submit his/her findings in a report or memo to the SAS Director.
3.) If there is no particular complaint to an incident, but the Immediate Academic Head has received a report thereof or such an incident has come to his/her knowledge, he/she shall immediately conduct a factfinding inquiry in order to protect the rights and interests of the University and of the affected individuals. If the result thereof establishes a conclusion of a probable commission of a misconduct, offense, infraction or violation that requires a disciplinary administrative investigation, he/she will submit his/her findings in a report or memo to the Director of the Student Affairs and Services.
4. Duty of the Director of the Student
Affairs and Services
a. The Director of the Office of the Student Affairs and Services will evaluate and determine whether or not there is still a need to further clarify certain matters, or additional facts must still be obtained. Hence, the Director of the Student Affairs and Services shall do any of the following:
1.) If there is still a need to further clarify certain alleged matters, or if additional facts must still be obtained, the Director of the Office of the Student Affairs and Services will refer back the matter to the Immediate Academic
Head for further fact-finding inquiry, that is, meetings and interviews of persons having knowledge of the surrounding circumstances, requiring their statements to be put into writing or affidavit. Later on, if the finding is that a misconduct, offense, infraction or violation had probably been committed by a certain student, the Immediate Academic Head shall make a written memo/report thereof to the Director of the Office of the Student Affairs and Services for appropriate action.
2.) If the alleged facts are clear and there is sufficient evidence that respondent probably committed the alleged misconduct, offense, infraction or violation, or the
Immediate Academic Head already submitted a subsequent memo or report with a finding that the alleged misconduct, offense, infraction or violation had probably been committed by respondent, the Director of the Student Affairs and Services shall do any of the following:
a.) If the misconduct, offense, infraction or violation is sanctionable by
 WARNING or
REPRIMAND, the Office of the Student Affairs and Services shall be the
Investigating Officer and shall proceed with the conduct of the administrative disciplinary investigation,
starting from issuance of the
 Notice of
Investigation
addressed to complainant and respondent, copy furnished the offices of the President and VP Academic Affairs.
b.) If the misconduct, offense, infraction or violation is sanctionable by SUSPENSION,
EXCLUSION or EXPULSION, the Director of the Office of the Student Affairs and Services shall refer the matter by memo to the Office of the
President,
through the VP Academic Affairs, requesting that the BOARD OF DISCIPLINE be convened to conduct the
investigation, indicating therein the name of complainant and respondent, the general description of the alleged misconduct, offense, infraction or violation to be investigated, and attaching thereto the available evidence (reports, affidavits and/or written
statements of witnesses, and other papers, documents or things, if any).
B. Preventive Suspension Pending Investigation
Section 1. At the start or at any stage of the investigation process before the final decision, the Director of the Student
Affairs and Services, motu proprio or upon recommendation of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, the College President or the Board of Discipline, may place a student to be investigated or already under investigation under preventive suspension for a period not prohibited by the Commission on Higher Education rules and regulations.
Section 2. The preventive suspension period served to a student shall be deducted from the penalty of suspension that may later be imposed on the student, if any. However, in the event that a student is found innocent, the period of preventive suspension shall not be counted against the students and he shall be allowed to take the missed examination missed and submit the missed subject requirements, if any.
C. Notice of Investigation; Answering of Respondent Section 1. The Director of the Office of the Student Affairs and Services or the Board of Discipline shall issue a Notice of Investigation to respondent student stating therein the following:
a. the alleged misconduct, offense, infraction or violation in general terms against him/her, furnishing him/her a copy of the complaint and the attachments thereto, if any;
b. the law, policy, rule or regulation being violated with corresponding sanction;
c. the date, time and place where the initial conference/hearing will be conducted;
d. the requirement for him/her to submit his/her written answer/ explanation and supporting documents, if any, and to furnish a copy thereof to the other party (complainant) through the Investigator within five (5) working days from receipt of the said notice;
e. the reminder of his/her rights to be represented by counsel if he/ she so desires, to examine the evidence against him/her, and to present evidence on his/her own behalf; and
f. the notice that if respondent student refuses or fails to submit his/her answer/explanation, such refusal shall be deemed a waiver to present evidence on his/her own behalf, and the investigation will proceed and will be decided based on the evidence adduced during the investigation.
D. Notification of Complainant for Parents or Guardians
Section 1. The Board of Discipline thru the Office of the Student Affairs and Services shall furnish a copy of the Notice of Investigation to complainant. If it is a student who is complaining without assistance from his/her parent/s or guardian, the Board of Discipline shall notify his/her parent/s or guardian accordingly at their last known address per school records. If the parent/s or guardian cannot be contacted or fail to come during the investigation despite the notice, the investigation shall proceed accordingly.
E. Initial Conference/Hearing
Section 1. During the initial conference/hearing, the Office of the Student Affairs and Services shall determine whether there is a prima facie case to proceed further with the investigation or dismiss the complaint or terminate the proceedings. It is well to note that the veracity or truthfulness of the allegations of complainant and respondent will only be determined by the Board of Discipline when he/she renders his/her decision in the resolution. Moreover, the issues will be clarified, stipulations and admissions will be made, or the parties will explore the possibility of settling amicably the personal claims of the complainant, if any, without prejudice to the respondent being investigated further to determine whether or not respondent is liable for having violated any of the College policies, rules or regulations, and the appropriate formative intervention thereto, if any.
Section 2. In the event that before or during the scheduled initial conference/hearing respondent admits in writing the allegations against him/her, or the facts are clear to the Board of Discipline, the case may be deemed submitted for decision based on the complaint and the answer unless the Board of Discipline will require submission of position papers.
F. Summary Judgement
Section 1. If on the basis of the documents submitted (such as the letter, report, answer, supporting papers and other evidence), the Board of Discipline finds that there is already sufficient basis to render judgment (as when the facts and issues are already clear to the Board of Discipline or when there is admission of guilt), it may immediately render summary judgment during the initial conference, or it may consider the case submitted for decision, and the parties shall be informed accordingly of the resulting written resolution.
G. Judgement Based on Position Papers
Section 1. Whenever summary judgment is not appropriate, the Board of Discipline shall direct the parties to the case to simultaneously submit their position papers with written statements or affidavits of witnesses and other supporting evidence within three (3) working days from date of the initial conference/hearing where the directive is given, or if given later after from notice of the order, after which the case shall be deemed submitted for decision. If one party refuses or fails to submit his/her position paper and additional supporting evidence, the same shall be deemed a waiver on the part of that party to present further evidence, and the case shall be decided based on whatever documents or evidence found in the record.
Section 2. In case the written statements of witnesses and parties are not notarized, the individuals concerned shall be required to appear before the Board of Discipline to affirm or swear on the veracity of their written allegations.
H. Judgement After Further Hearing
Section 1. Where the Board of Discipline finds that there are complicated factual issues involved which cannot be resolved through position papers, or which need further clarification for better understanding, or there are other witnesses who may be called or presented to testify to shed light on certain factual issues, it shall conduct further hearing. The Board of Discipline, if necessary, shall direct the parties and other persons to appear before it to answer classificatory questions. Any employee or student who refuses to attend and testify in the hearing shall be reported to the Office of the Vice President for Administration or HRMD or Office of the Student Affairs and Services for appropriate action. For this purpose, the Board of Discipline will then proceed to ask questions first to complainant and his/her witnesses, and second to respondent and his/her witnesses. After a witness has been asked by the Board of Discipline, any of the contending parties or their counsel, if represented, may examine further the witness by submitting written questions to the Board of Discipline, who will then read the questions to the witness for his answers. However, the Investigator may allow the counsel to directly ask the questions to the witness. Minutes summarizing the proceedings shall be in writing and signed by the Board of Discipline, the parties, and their counsels, if any.
I. Resolution of the Case, Finality of
Resolution/Decision, Motion for Reconsideration, and Appeal.
Section 1. The Board of Discipline shall decide the case within fifteen (15) working days from the last hearing or on the date stated in its Order stating that the case is deemed submitted for decision (for instances when position papers are required to be submitted before judgment). The resolution should be based on the evidence adduced during the investigation and the applicable law, policies, rules or regulations. The resolution must contain these essential parts:
1. statement of the case;
2. finding of facts, issues;
3. discussions of the issues, applicable laws, policies, rules and/or regulation; and
4. dispositive portion with recommended formative intervention to be imposed or appropriate action to be taken. The parties shall be furnished a copy each of the resolution.
Section 2. The Board of Discipline may ask for extension of the period to decide on a valid ground. The Office of the College President may extend the period for the Board of Discipline to decide the case if it will find the ground relied upon by the Investigator to be valid and reasonable.
Section 3. If respondent is found liable, the possible formative intervention that may be recommended may either be Warning, Reprimand, Suspension, Exclusion or Expulsion. However, if a case involves theft, non-liquidation of funds, actual damages resulting from respondent’s act or negligence, or analogous cases, the resolution or decision may include the directive to return the stolen object or pay its value, or pay a specific sum of money.
Section 4. The resolution of the Board of Discipline is final unless appealed to the Office of the President within five (5) working days from receipt of the decision. A motion for reconsideration shall be considered an appeal. The appeal or motion for reconsideration, filed by any of the parties with the Board of Discipline, with a copy thereof furnished by the movant/appellant to the other party through the Board of Discipline, shall state the reason or reasons why the resolution of the Board of Discipline should be reversed, modified, or set aside, and a new one is to be rendered by the President.
Section 5. The other party (appellee) shall have three (3) working days from receipt of the motion or appeal within which to file his/her Comment or Opposition to the said motion or appeal. After the lapse of the period to submit the Comment or Opposition, with or without the opposition, the Office of the College President shall review the records of the case and render decision based on the evidence adduced during the investigation and the applicable laws, policies, rules and/or regulations, either affirming, reversing, modifying, or setting aside the resolution of the Board of Discipline and render a new one, or directing whatever the College President may deem necessary and proper.
Section 6. The decision of the Office of the College President is immediately final and executory upon issuance thereof, unless otherwise stated therein.
J. Action of the President on Unappealed Resolution Section 1. If the resolution of the Board of Discipline is not appealed within the reglementary period, said resolution shall be immediately endorsed to the Office of the College President for its final determination whether or not to approve its execution or for whatever action it may deem necessary and proper (such as to order a reinvestigation, or to review and render a new decision modifying or amending the previous one). The action of the Office of the College President shall constitute the final decision.
K. Furnishing Copy of Resolution or Decision
Section 1. Complainant, respondent and the student’s/students’ parent/s or guardian/s shall each be furnished a copy of the resolution or decision through the Office of the Student Affairs and Services, by personal service or by special mail delivery through private courier (such as LBC, JRS or DHL), or by registered mail at their last known addresses per school records.
L. Student Misconduct Record (SMR)
Section 1. After finality of the resolution/decision, the Director of the Office of the Student Affairs and Services prepares the Student Misconduct Record (SMR) in four (4) copies describing the nature of the infraction and quoting the dispositive portion of the final resolution/decision.
Section 2. Copies of the SMR shall be distributed as follows:
1. First copy - Respondent student
2. Second copy - Dean or Program Head of respondent student
3. Third copy - Department Guidance Office
4. Fourth copy – Office of the Student Affairs and Services
M. Court Action Against Respondent Student
Section 1. The administrative investigation or the formative intervention meted shall not prejudice the right of the College, the complainant or the victim to initiate court action against the respondent student if warranted and opted by the former.

ARTICLE VIII EDUCATION TOUR/FIELD POLICIES AND GUIDELINE
The primary objective of the school field trips is to provide an educational experience in keeping with planned curriculum, while exposing students to new cultural and physical opportunities not found in daily life. Moreover, field trips are designed to encourage group participation and bonding among the students and teachers. With those objectives in mind, the following guidelines have been designed to help students, teacher, chaperones, and parents get the most of their field trip experience.
A. Student’s Roles
Section 1. All students are expected to participate in field trips but not forcibly imposed.
Section 2. Because field trips are an opportunity for students to stretch themselves in new and unique ways, Students should show a positive attitude when facing unfamiliar situations or challenges.
Section 3. Throughout the field trip, students are expected to uphold regular school rules and show respect for each other, teacher and other adult supervisor.
Section 4. During a field trip, students are representative of our institution, so their behavior should reflect that at all times.
Section 5. Field trips begin at the designated meeting place (usually the town bus or ferry terminal) if a student requires alternative arrival, departure, or other transportation arrangements, parents must notify teacher in writing prior to the trip.
B. Teacher’s Roles
Section 1. Teachers are to design field trip experiences that appropriately dovetail with the existing curriculum, provide unique experiences are age appropriate for the students participating, and are of reasonable cost.
Section 2. Teachers shall determine the number of chaperones needed for a field trip.
Section 3. Teachers shall coordinate with the transportation to and from the event, assess costs, assign chaperone duties, and make other logistical arrangements well in advance of the field trip.
Section 4. Teachers shall then communicate those plans to the College President for Board of Trustees’ approval.
Section 5. Once a field trip has been organized and approved, teacher shall be responsible for fund raising and communicating logistical plans to parents and obtaining permission slips from them.
C. Personnel In-Charge
Section 1. The role of the Personnel In-Charge (PIC) is to support teachers and to provide additional supervision for the entire group of students, as needed. They may be called on to perform a variety of roles, depending on the nature of the trip.
Section 2. PIC support the educational or cultural nature of the event and should provide a positive example of the students.
Section 3. They are to work with the entire group or with a small group of students, as directed by the teachers.
Section 4. Prior to and throughout the trip, PIC should be in communication with teachers to determine specific roles and responsibilities.
Section 5. PIC help teachers monitor student behavior and refer any issues to teachers.
Section 6. Students are under the direct supervision of the teacher in-charge at all times.
Section 7. During overnight field trips, PIC is responsible for student supervision 24 hours a day, unless otherwise determined by teachers, and should remain with the group throughout the entire field trips.
Section 8. PIC may not bring non-students on the trip.
Section 9. PIC should not smoke in the presence of students or any enclosed areas.
Section 10. PIC shall not drink alcohol or use illegal drugs at any time.
Section 11. PIC, who drive their personal vehicles, carrying students, must provide evidence of liability insurance and a valid driver’s license.
D. Parents’ Participants
Section 1. If a parent wants to go on a school trip to provide additional support for his or her own son/daughter due to a certain situation like having special needs, this may be permissible given the following guidelines:
1. Parent participants should consult with teacher prior to the trip to determine the level of participation that is appropriate.
2. Any additional expenses that a parent’s presence incurs, including lodging, food, admission to events or programs, and travel expenses, will be the parents’ responsibility.
3. In order to avoid potential disruptions or distractions, parents are discouraged from bringing pre-school siblings of students.
4. In the interest of preserving the objectives of the field trip and enhancing their son’s/daughter’s experience as a part of the group parent participants may not remove their son/daughter activities, including transportation to and from the event, except in true emergency situations.
5. Parent participants are not to smoke in the presence of students or in any enclosed areas.
6. Parent participants are not to drink alcohol or use illegal drugs at any time.
7. Parent participants who drive their own vehicles assume all liabilities.
E. Checklist of Requirements
Section 1. Before the Educational Visit/Tour/Trip
1. Permission Letter from the Personnel In Charge to the President (with the signature from the Dean of the requesting party Office of the Student Affairs and Services. Vice President for Academic Affairs)
2. Attached to the Permission Letter is the curriculum where field trip is required and a particular syllabus of the subject which needs a field trip to enhance the subject matter with or allotted grade as part of the grading system can be found in the Student’s Handbook approved by the Board of Trustees and be presented every General Orientation among freshman students.
3. Copy of the approval letter offices/companies/plants where the tour will be conducted.
4. Fill up the Activity Permit Form to hold Educational Field Trips from the Tour Coordinator.
5. Itinerary of the Tour (approved by the Dean of the requesting party, noted by the VPAA and attested by the President).
6. Attendance Sheet/List of students with their signatures who are joining the trip Waiver/Parent’s consent.
7. Budget/Funding Resources
8. Copy of Insurance Policy with the list of students concerned stakeholders.
9. Medical clearance of students.
10. List of the teachers/chaperones (I faculty/staff for every 50 students)
Section 2. After the Educational Visit/Tour/Trip
1. Duly signed and accomplished Attendance Sheet including the attendance before leaving the campus, during the educational tour, and arrival at the campus.
2. Learning journal of students highlighting the essential lessons and learning they have.
3. Evaluation result form.

Section 3. If you are provided with an establishment’s rules, read and follow strictly.
Section 4. Strictly follow instructions/assignments given to you by your supervisor.
Section 5. Obey your supervisor and do not show insubordination to him.
Section 6. Always give prior notice to your supervisor if you will be absent or late for duty. Excuses for such should be reasonable.
Section 7. Be careful and show enthusiasm while doing your work.

ARTICLE X TRANSITORY PROVISIONS
Section 1. Repealing Clause. Any provisions of this Student Manual or any part thereof that are found to be contrary to or inconsistent with the Philippine Constitution or with laws, decrees, rules and regulations are deemed null and void.
Section 2. Separability Clause. If any part, chapter or section or provision of this Student Manual shall be held unconstitutional, no other part, chapter, section or provisions thereof shall be affected thereby.

DATA PRIVACY CONSENT FORM
Statement of Privacy Policy
TALIBON POLYTECHNIC COLLEGE (TPC) is committed to protecting the privacy of its data subjects, and ensuring the safety and security of personal data under its control and custody. This policy provides information on what personal data is gathered by TPC about its current, past, and prospective students; how it will use and process this; how it will keep this secure; and how it will dispose of it when it is no longer needed. This information is provided in compliance with the Philippine Republic Act No. 10173, also known as, the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA) and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (DPA-IRR). It sets out TPC’s data protection practices designed to safeguard the personal data of individuals it deals with, and also to inform such individuals of their rights under the Act.
This Data Privacy Notice and Consent Form may be amended at any time without prior notice, and such amendments will be notified to you via TPC’s website or by email.
Privacy Notice
Information Collected
TALIBON POLYTECHNIC COLLEGE collects, stores, and processes personal data from its current, past and prospective students, starting with the information provided at application through to information collected throughout the whole course of study at the College. This will include:
1. Contact information, such as, name, addresses, telephone numbers, email addresses and other contact details
2. Personal information, such as date and place of birth, nationality, immigration status, religion, civil status, student ID, government-issued IDs, web information, recommendations and assessment forms from previous schools, etc.
3. Family background, including information on parents, guardians, siblings, related TPC alumnae, etc.
4. Photographic and biometric data, such as, photos, CCTV videos, fingerprints, handwriting and signature specimens
5. Student's school works, including data gathered using third party online learning tools, such as, Schoology and other related.
6. Health records, psychological evaluation results, disciplinary records, and physical fitness information
7. Student Cumulative Guidance Folder, which includes interviews, entrance exam results, guidance assessments, special needs, exclusions/behavioral information, etc.
8. Permanent Student Academic Records, including transcripts and the academic history of the student in TPC.
9. Student extra-curricular activities, résumés, job interview forms
10. Financial and billing information
Use of Information
The collected personal data is used solely for the following purposes:
1. Processing of admission application and student selection (and to confirm the identity of prospective students and their parents)
2. Verifying authenticity of student records and documents
3. Processing of scholarship applications and its ongoing requirements
4. Processing of enrollment and registration
5. Supporting student learning, and validating students’ program of study based on curriculum requirements, and other activities and experiences forming part of the student’s formation and education.
6. Supporting the student’s well-being and providing medical services and guidance counselling
7. Monitoring and reporting on student progress; processing of evaluations, exam results, and grades
8. Monitoring and ensuring the safety of all students within the TPC campus
9. Processing and generating statements of accounts
10. Processing of application for graduation
11. Evaluation for board examinations
12. Documentation of students’ data
13. For accreditation, professional development of teachers and staff, and research, e.g., evaluation studies by the research desk, action research by teachers, etc.
14. Posting or displaying of academic and non-academic achievements within the TPC’s premises and/or its official website and social media accounts and/or school publication
15. Marketing and promoting TPC, its students, employees, and other academic and non-academic student and/or school activities inside and outside the campus
16. Providing Library services, running an outreach program, family council purposes, job postings, practicums, internships, employment
Information Sharing
Personal data under the custody of TPC shall be disclosed only to authorized recipients of such data. Otherwise, we will share your personal data with third parties, other than your parents and/or guardian on record for minors, only with your consent, or when required or permitted by our policies and applicable law, such as with:
1. Regulatory authorities, courts, and government agencies, e.g., Commission on Higher Education, etc.
2. Service Providers who perform services for us and help us support your learning, monitor and report on your progress, manage the operations of our school, and assess how well TPC is doing.
3. Business partners and other academic linkages who provide internships and job opportunities to our graduates.
Data Transfer
Where TPC consider it necessary or appropriate, for the purposes of data storage, processing, providing any service or product on our behalf to you, or implementing an academic linkage program, we may transfer your personal data to third parties within or outside of the Philippines, under conditions of confidentiality and similar levels of security safeguards.
Security
1. We continue to implement organizational, administrative, technical, and physical security measures to safeguard your personal data.
2. Only authorized personnel have access to your personal data, the exchange of which (mainly within campus) is facilitated through internal shared servers, email, and paper files.
3. Should third parties need access to your personal data, we require some form of data sharing agreement with them, in compliance with the DPA and the DPA-IRR.
4. Your paper and digital files are securely stored: employing physical security to safeguard the paper files and technical security to protect the digital files.
Retention of Information
We keep your paper and digital files only for as long as necessary.
